hints: Focus on what an ester of methanoic acid must look like, it always contains the HCOO group joined to an alkyl group.
Subtract HCOO from C5H10O2 to find the alkyl group attached to oxygen, you are left with four different butyl skeletons to draw.
Check each butyl formate for a chiral carbon, one of them can exist as a pair of non-superimposable mirror images so counts twice.
walkthrough:
**Recognise a methanoate ester**

All esters of methanoic acid have the same formate part. Think of it as HCOO-R.

$$\text{H-C(=O)-O-R}$$

**Find the R group from the formula**

The whole ester is $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2$. Remove $\text{HCOO}$ which is $\text{CHO}_2$.

$$\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_2 - \text{CHO}_2 = \text{C}_4\text{H}_9$$
So R is a $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$ butyl group.

**Count structural butyl isomers**

There are 4 different ways to arrange $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9$ as an alcohol residue:
1. $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (butyl)
2. $\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ (sec-butyl)
3. $\text{-CH}_2\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)}_2$ (2-methylpropyl)
4. $\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)}_3$ (tert-butyl)
That gives 4 structural formate esters.

**Add stereoisomerism**

Look for a chiral centre. In sec-butyl methanoate, $\text{HCOO-CH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, the carbon joined to O is bonded to H, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{OCOH}$.
That is four different groups, so it is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers. The other three have no chiral centre.

Total = 3 single isomers + 2 enantiomers = 5 isomeric esters.

options.A: 2 is far too low. It might come from counting only straight chain and branched primary alcohols and forgetting sec-butyl and tert-butyl structures completely.
options.B: 3 is too low. It might come from missing one or more of the branched butyl skeletons, for example forgetting the tertiary alcohol residue.
options.C: 4 counts the structural isomers correctly but misses the stereoisomerism clue. Sec-butyl methanoate is chiral and counts as two enantiomers, not one.
options.D: 5 is correct. The four butyl groups give four structural methanoates, and sec-butyl methanoate is chiral so adds one extra enantiomer, giving 3 + 2 = 5 in total.
